title: Task Relation-aware Continual User Representation Learning

problem.claim: User representation learning must support multiple tasks and continually added tasks while retaining previously learned knowledge.

gap.claim: Existing universal user representation approaches are impractical because of data requirements, catastrophic forgetting, and limited learning capability as tasks are added.

contributions.claim: TERACON is a continual user representation learning method designed to capture relationships among tasks while maintaining learning capability as the number of learned tasks increases.
TERACON uses task embeddings to generate task-specific soft masks that keep the entire model parameter set updateable through the training sequence and capture task relationships.
TERACON introduces a knowledge retention module with a pseudo-labeling strategy to alleviate catastrophic forgetting.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly describe TERACON and its knowledge retention module as novel.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report extensive experiments on public and proprietary real-world datasets.
The authors report that these experiments demonstrate TERACON's superiority and practicality.
The authors report that the code is available online.

narrative_sequence.summary: User modeling represents users in a low-dimensional space from past behavior to support personalized services.
Earlier work focused mainly on task-specific representations, while later work introduced universal representations relevant to multiple tasks.
Existing universal representation methods face data requirements, catastrophic forgetting, and limited capability for continually added tasks.
TERACON addresses the gap with task embeddings, task-specific soft masks, and a pseudo-labeling-based knowledge retention module.
Experiments on public and proprietary real-world datasets are reported to demonstrate superiority and practicality.
